Predict a geographically weighted regression at new locations

Source: R/gwr-predict.R
ef_gwr_predict.Rd

Exact GWR prediction: at each new location g with covariates \(x_g\), weights with respect to the stations of the fit (same kernel and bandwidth; adaptive: the k-th smallest distance from g to the stations), local WLS fit and $$\hat y_g = x_g^\top \hat\beta_g, \qquad \hat\beta_g = (X^\top W_g X)^{-1} X^\top W_g y$$ (dev/specs/gwr-forcing.md sections 3.2 and 6.1). Designed to be called on blocks of rows (e.g. one raster block at a time): rows are processed independently, so the result does not depend on how the locations are split into calls or chunks.

Usage

ef_gwr_predict(object, newx, newcoords, chunk_rows = 10000L)

Arguments

object

An earthflux_gwr object from ef_gwr_fit().

newx

Numeric matrix (or data frame) of covariates at the new locations, one row per location, with the same column names (and units) as the covariates of the fit; column order may differ.

newcoords

Numeric matrix with two columns: projected coordinates (x, y) of the new locations [m], in the CRS of the fit.

chunk_rows

Whole number: rows processed together internally. It only bounds memory (about 8 x chunk_rows x n bytes per matrix of distances or weights) and never changes the result.

Value

A list with:

  • value: numeric vector of predictions, in the unit of the response; NA where a covariate or coordinate is missing or the local design is rank deficient;

  • coefficients: matrix (rows x p) of local coefficients in original units (NA rows as for value);

  • bandwidth: bandwidth used at each location [m];

  • n_nonzero: integer number of neighbours of each location (stations with a non-zero weight for compact kernels, within one bandwidth for the gaussian and exponential kernels);

  • flags: list of earthflux_flag records (cell scope; index = positions in the rows of this call) with the attribute evaluated.

Details

Flags (cell scope, bits of the GWR flag word, dev/specs/flags.md 6.4):

  • EF_INPUT_NA (bit 0): a covariate or coordinate is missing;

  • EF_GWR_EXTRAPOLATION_COVARIATE (bit 1): some covariate is outside the range [min, max] of the stations used in the fit;

  • EF_GWR_EXTRAPOLATION_LOCAL (bit 2): some covariate is outside the range of the stations with a non-zero weight at the location; evaluated only for the compact kernels (bisquare, tricube, boxcar);

  • EF_GWR_OUTSIDE_HULL (bit 3): the location is outside the convex hull of the stations used (points on its boundary are inside);

  • EF_GWR_FEW_NEIGHBOURS (bit 4): fewer neighbours than the min_neighbours of the fit; the value is kept;

  • EF_GWR_LOCAL_SINGULAR (bit 5): the local design is rank deficient; the value and coefficients are NA (never replaced by OLS or a neighbour).

The distance to the nearest station (EF_GWR_FAR_FROM_STATIONS) needs a threshold without reference (class II) and is not evaluated.

Errors: earthflux_input_error (columns of newx not matching the covariates of the fit, newcoords not with two columns, row counts differing, no rows); earthflux_domain_error (infinite values).

Verification status

As ef_gwr_fit(): estimator CANDIDATA (corroborada); the predictions agree with GWmodel::gwr.predict() to 1e-10 relative in the cross-check tests. The extrapolation conditions are design definitions without threshold (dev/specs/gwr-forcing.md section 6.3).

See also

Other spatial regionalization functions: ef_gwr_bandwidth(), ef_gwr_diagnostics(), ef_gwr_fit(), ef_gwr_search(), ef_method_gwr(), ef_method_idw(), ef_method_ols(), ef_method_station(), ef_predict_control(), ef_regionalize(), ef_regionalize_cv(), ef_spatial_folds()

Examples

coords <- cbind(c(0, 10000, 0, 10000, 20000, 30000),
                c(0, 0, 10000, 10000, 0, 30000))
elev <- cbind(elevation = c(100, 300, 500, 200, 800, 1200))
ta <- c(20.0, 18.9, 17.5, 19.6, 15.4, 13.1)
fit <- ef_gwr_fit(ta, elev, coords, bandwidth = 20000,
                  kernel = "gaussian")
cells <- cbind(c(5000, 15000, 40000), c(5000, 5000, 40000))
pred <- ef_gwr_predict(fit, cbind(elevation = c(250, 600, 1500)), cells)
pred$value
#> [1] 19.14890 16.85496 11.16064
vapply(pred$flags, `[[`, "", "code")
#> [1] "EF_GWR_EXTRAPOLATION_COVARIATE" "EF_GWR_OUTSIDE_HULL"           
#> [3] "EF_GWR_FEW_NEIGHBOURS"
